product.name: surf
product.eyebrow: Web browser · written from scratch · early
promise: A web browser written from scratch,
product.lede: surf is a small browser written in Rust. It does not wrap Chromium, WebKit or Gecko, and nothing that ships depends on a third-party crate. Every behaviour is written down as a specification before any code exists, and a test suite generated from that specification runs against the real code on every change.
product.meta: Rust · ESS specification · headless command line · not a browser for daily use

art.caption: surf loads one address and prints one line per thing that happened. The exit status says whether the page loaded.

sections.title: A browser built from first principles.
sections.lede: surf is young. Today it loads a page from the command line and tells you what happened. There is no window, no rendering, no JavaScript and no https: yet.

items.title: Written here
items.description: URL parsing, HTTP, HTML parsing and everything after them are written in this repository, each against its standard.

items.title: Components that share no state
items.description: Each component keeps its own data, accepts commands and publishes events. Nothing reaches into another component's memory.

items.title: Headless first
items.description: Its first interface is a command line, for people and for agents.

items.title: No runtime dependencies
items.description: An experiment: how far does a browser get with no third-party code in what ships?

items.title: swell, the script engine
items.description: An ECMAScript (JavaScript) engine written from scratch in Rust, a project of its own that surf will embed. surf runs no script today.

sections.title: From a specification to code that is held to it.
sections.lede: The design lives in spec/ as an ESS specification. One command, task check, checks every step.

steps.label: Specify
steps.title: spec/
steps.description: Every behaviour is stated before any code for it exists.

steps.label: Generate
steps.title: generated/rust/
steps.description: ess generates the components and the scenarios that hold the code to the specification.

steps.label: Supply
steps.title: crates/
steps.description: Hand-written crates add the network, each component's storage and the command line.

steps.label: Check
steps.title: task check
steps.description: The scenarios run against the specification's interpreter and against the Rust code, then the build and the tests.
